:coffee: *Breakfast Briefing — Thursday 10 September* is out (automated): <https://docs.google.com/document/d/1yXqkDR051M6EO3K3g37K_gW9vYeT2C3_iiWcUnhd3Zs/edit|docs.google.com/document/d/1yXqkDR051M6EO3K3g3…/edit>

Top five for the UK:

1. *<https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-16117951/Badenoch-vote-against-assisted-dying-law-returns-Commons-week-Tory-leader-warns-MPs-clear-eyed-Bills-fatal-flaws.html|Badenoch to vote against assisted dying law when it returns to Commons this week as Tory leader warns MPs to be 'clear-eyed' about Bill's 'fatal flaws'>* — Mail. Second Reading is *tomorrow, Friday 11 September*.
    ◦ <https://spectator.com/article/the-assisted-dying-vote-is-a-test-of-labours-core-values|The assisted dying vote is a test of Labour’s core values> — The Spectator. Lois McLatchie Miller on whether Labour MPs still hold to protecting the vulnerable
    ◦ <https://www.christian.org.uk/features/assisted-suicide-is-just-like-abortion-lauren-edwards-advocacy-for-death-by-choice|‘Assisted suicide is just like abortion’: Lauren Edwards’ advocacy for death by ‘choice’> — The Christian Institute, on the Bill sponsor's own comparison in her latest opinion piece
    ◦ <https://thecatholicherald.com/article/assisted-suicide-vote-to-follow-world-suicide-prevention-day|Assisted suicide vote to follow World Suicide Prevention Day> — The Catholic Herald. A government suicide-prevention adviser questions the contrast. Today is the day itself
2. *<https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9w41v2r742o|Drug gangs exploited and raped us as teens, then police failed us, women tell BBC>* — BBC. Four women waive anonymity for the documentary *Britain's Forgotten Girls*: groomed as children, then not taken seriously by the authorities.
3. *<https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-16118541/M-iri-McAllan-comes-fire-having-no-ambition-unable-guarantee-standards-schools-improve-2029.html|Màiri McAllan comes under fire for having no ambition after she was unable to guarantee standards in schools will improve by 2029>* — Mail. The 2025 PISA data has England in the top ten while Scotland and Wales slump.
    ◦ <https://theconversation.com/pisa-results-what-they-tell-us-about-reading-standards-in-welsh-schools-and-what-they-dont-291381|Pisa results: what they tell us about reading standards in Welsh schools – and what they don’t> — The Conversation – Articles (UK). Nearly one in three Welsh pupils missed the baseline
4. *<https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/nigel-farage-face-coverings-migrant-protests-b1296098.html|Farage calls for ban on face coverings in public after anti-migration protests>* — London Evening Standard. Prompted by the masked protesters at Dover and Portsmouth, but drawn much wider.
    ◦ <https://www.spiked-online.com/2026/09/09/why-ban-balaclavas-but-not-burqas|Why ban balaclavas, but not burqas?> — spiked, on Nottingham's new face-covering powers, which take effect next week
    ◦ <https://www.gbnews.com/news/london-no-go-zones-sharia-law-third-of-britons|More than a third of Britons fear 'no-go zones' in London where sharia law dominates> — GB News.
5. *<https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-16116949/Residents-tiny-Oxfordshire-village-centre-migrant-crisis-fear-asylum-seeker-camp-DOUBLE-size-house-3-510-men.html|Residents in tiny Oxfordshire village at centre of migrant crisis fear asylum seeker camp could DOUBLE in size to house 3,510 men>* — Mail. The village has 350 residents, 46 of them children.
    ◦ <https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cly47p5vk63o|RNLI volunteer targeted online and branded 'traitor' after Portsmouth protests> — BBC.

304 stories across nine sections in the Doc — worth a scroll for the rest.
